title: Ports of Plague
subtitle: A game of trade, survival and conscience during the Black Death, 1347–1353

blocks.text: In 1346 plague broke out among the Mongol army besieging the Genoese port of Caffa on the Black Sea {{fact:TR-02}}. Italian merchant ships carried it to Constantinople, then to Sicily in October 1347 {{fact:TR-06}}, and from there along the trade routes to almost every corner of Europe by 1353 {{fact:TL-02}} {{fact:TR-10}}. Somewhere between a third and 60 percent of Europeans died; historians still debate the number {{fact:DB-01}}.

You lead a merchant family in one of Europe's great trading cities. Trade makes you rich, but every ship can carry the plague. The game follows the real timeline: the plague reaches each city in the half-year it really did. Along the way you will face the same choices real people faced: to flee or to stay, to trust physicians who could not cure the disease {{fact:ME-08}}, to answer the Church's call, to obey or ignore England's wage laws {{fact:EC-05}}, and whether to stand up for neighbors falsely blamed for the plague {{fact:SO-07}}.

A standard game lasts **{{rounds}} rounds** of half a year each, from Late 1347 to Early 1353; **Quick Play** covers the same years in 6 rounds of a whole year. When it ends, the house with the highest **Legacy score** wins. Legacy combines **Wealth**, **Family** and **Reputation**, plus a **Balance bonus** equal to your weakest of the three. A balanced house usually beats a greedy one. No one is ever knocked out of the game.

items: **The map**: 25 real cities joined by sea routes (solid lines) and land routes (dashed lines). Each route shows its base value.

**City markers**: *Safe* (plain). *Safe* cities can also be *Threatened* (dashed orange ring: a neighbouring city is Stricken). *Stricken* cities have a red ring, a hatched centre and 1–3 severity pips; *Aftermath* cities have a grey ring and a ❦ mark.

**House crests**: each player has a color and a shape (circle, square, triangle, diamond, hexagon or star). A banner by a city is a trading post; the number on it shows how many family members live there.
**Dice**: turn-order, profit, contagion, severity and mortality dice, all rolled by the computer with animation.
**Cards**: dated *Chronicle* cards, a shuffled deck of 34 *Event* cards, and a personal deck of 22 *Fortune* cards.
**Tracks and Journal**: florins (ƒ), reputation (0–{{limits.maxReputation}}), family, a live Legacy score, and the Historian's Journal of every fact you meet, with its source.

Choose {{players.min}}–{{players.max}} players. Each picks a house name and a different home city (Venice, Genoa, Florence, Marseille, Barcelona, London, Bruges or Lübeck). Colors and crests are assigned by seat.

Each house starts with **{{start.florins}} florins**, **{{start.family}} family members** in the home city, **{{start.reputation}} reputation** and **one trading post** in the home city. To balance their routes and plague dates, home cities start with slightly different amounts of money, shown on the setup screen.
Choose **Standard** or **Quick Play**, and a difficulty: **Apprentice** (gentler plague, hints all game), **Chronicler** (standard) or **Great Mortality** (severity rolls +1, contagion risk +1).
Caffa begins Stricken. Each house rolls a die: the highest goes first and tied houses roll again. **This turn order stays the same all game.**
**Chronicle.** The date advances. The plague reaches every city whose real arrival date falls in this round; each becomes Stricken and rolls severity. Then the round's dated Chronicle cards are read.
**Event.** One Event card is drawn. If it offers a choice, each player decides at the start of their own turn.

**Actions.** Players take turns in the fixed order, each with **{{modes.standard.actionPoints}} action points (AP)** ({{modes.quick.actionPoints}} in Quick Play). A pass-the-device screen appears between turns.
**Plague & upkeep.** Family members in Stricken cities roll for survival. Cities Stricken for {{plague.strickenRounds}} half-years move to Aftermath.

blocks.text: Quick Play: each round covers two half-years at once, so arrivals and Chronicle cards for both are read, and the plague phase happens twice (two survival rolls).

Pick a city where your family lives. They shut themselves in and stockpile food, the way some families isolated themselves in 1348 {{fact:SO-05}}. This round their survival rolls there get +{{plague.prepareBonus}}.

blocks.text: The game blocks illegal moves and explains why, for example: "Florence is Stricken: its gates are closed to new trading posts."

items: **Historical spread.** At the start of each round, the plague reaches the cities it really reached in that half-year. The date and its source are shown in a Historical Note.

**Severity.** Each newly Stricken city rolls the severity die: 1–2 **Light** (1 pip), 3–4 **Heavy** (2), 5–6 **Devastating** (3). Hard-hit Tuscany and Catalonia (Florence, Pisa, Barcelona) add 1; Flanders (Bruges) subtracts 1 {{fact:CI-06}}. On Apprentice difficulty, every roll is 1 lower (never below Light).

**Contagion.** When you ship from a Stricken city, the contagion die is rolled. If it is equal to or lower than that city's severity, the cargo is **infected**: you earn only half the profit (rounded down) and lose {{penalties.infectedCargoReputation}} reputation, as ports blamed plague ships {{fact:CI-11}}. If the destination is Safe and the plague really reached it in the *next* round, it becomes Stricken now, {{plague.earlyArrivalWindow}} round early. If the destination is already Stricken, its severity rises by 1 (maximum 3). Otherwise the infection dies out.

**Survival.** In the Plague phase, each family member in a Stricken city rolls the mortality die, adding +{{plague.prepareBonus}} if the household was prepared. If the result is equal to or lower than the severity, that family member dies.
**The last heir.** A house's last family member never dies; a distant cousin inherits. No one is eliminated.
**Inheritance.** For each family member lost, the house inherits {{gains.inheritance}}ƒ. Survivors really did inherit the property of the dead {{fact:EC-10}}.

**Aftermath.** After {{plague.strickenRounds}} rounds a Stricken city enters Aftermath. Workers are scarce and prices are high {{fact:EC-03}} {{fact:EC-04}}: shipping *from* it costs a wage, and shipping *to* it earns a bonus.
**Chronicle cards** are real, dated history and always appear in their round, for example the Ordinance of Labourers in Early 1349 {{fact:EC-05}} and the Jubilee of 1350 {{fact:CH-08}}.
**Event cards** are drawn one per round from a shuffled deck of 34, so each game is different. Some affect every house; some fall on one house chosen at random.

**Fortune cards** are personal. You draw one whenever you roll a {{fortune.drawOnProfitDie}} on the profit die or open a new trading post: spice cargoes, extra action points, free posts, warnings of where the plague goes next, but also demanding workers, illness and nervous creditors.
**Offers** ("Buy a Book of Hours?") are accepted or declined at the start of your turn (Fortune offers at once). Some offers are traps from history: the remedy seller's cure does nothing.

**Wage laws.** If you own a post in London or Melcombe Regis, choose: **Obey** (+{{wageLaw.obeyReputation}} reputation, but your English posts cannot ship this round, because workers refuse the old wages) or **Pay market wages** (roll a die: on 1–{{wageLaw.fineMaxRoll}} you are fined {{wageLaw.fine}}ƒ). The real laws failed to hold wages down {{fact:EC-07}}.

**Persecution.** The game shows the persecution of Jewish communities because it really happened, and because the accusations were **false** and the violence **unjust** {{fact:SO-07}} {{fact:SO-09}}. When it appears, any house may **Protect the Community** for {{costs.protectCommunity}}ƒ and 1 AP at the start of its turn, gaining {{gains.protectReputation}} reputation. No house can ever gain anything from persecution. Whatever players choose, the city suffers unrest: shipments to or from it earn {{penalties.unrestProfit}} less for {{penalties.unrestRounds}} rounds. Pope Clement VI condemned the accusations, but his words had little effect far from Avignon {{fact:SO-08}}.

blocks.text: Highest Legacy wins. Ties go to higher reputation, then more family; if still tied, the houses share the victory.

**Comebacks.** From round {{comeback.guildFavorFromRound}} on (counted in half-years), a house in last place that trails the leader by {{comeback.guildFavorMinGap}} or more Legacy points receives **Guild's Favor**: +{{comeback.guildFavorAP}} AP. Inheritance, the Survivors Marry chronicle and cheaper charity also help houses that fall behind.

items: **Round:** Chronicle → Event → Actions ({{modes.standard.actionPoints}} AP each; {{modes.quick.actionPoints}} in Quick Play) → Plague & upkeep. Turn order never changes.

**Ship:** route value + profit die + family {{gains.familyAtPostBonus}} + Aftermath destination {{gains.aftermathPriceBonus}} − Aftermath wage {{costs.wageAftermath}}. From a Stricken city: contagion die ≤ severity means infected (half profit, −{{penalties.infectedCargoReputation}} reputation, may spread). Profit die {{fortune.drawOnProfitDie}}: draw a Fortune card.
**Survival:** mortality die (+{{plague.prepareBonus}} if prepared) ≤ severity means the family member dies. The last heir always survives. Each loss inherits {{gains.inheritance}}ƒ.
**Costs:** Post {{costs.openPost}}ƒ · Prepare {{costs.prepareHousehold}}ƒ · Physician {{costs.physician}}ƒ · Charity {{costs.charity}}ƒ · Protect {{costs.protectCommunity}}ƒ + 1 AP.

Aftermath
A city the plague has passed through, now short of workers and with high prices. {{fact:EC-02}}
Bull (papal)
An official document from the pope, named after the metal seal attached to it. {{fact:CH-09}}
Cog / galley
Kinds of merchant ship: cogs sailed the northern seas, galleys the Mediterranean. {{fact:TR-04}} {{fact:TR-06}}
Flagellants
Penitents who marched between towns whipping themselves to beg God's mercy. {{fact:SO-02}}
Florin (ƒ)
A famous gold coin first minted in Florence in 1252. {{fact:EC-11}}
Hanseatic League
A network of German trading cities and their ships in the North Sea and Baltic. {{fact:TR-04}}
Humors
Body fluids that medieval doctors believed had to stay in balance. {{fact:ME-05}}
Miasma
"Bad air," wrongly believed to cause the plague. {{fact:ME-04}}
Quarantine
Isolation of travelers, first made law in Ragusa in 1377, after this game ends. {{fact:ME-14}}
Stricken
A city where the plague is raging. Severity: Light, Heavy or Devastating.
